vignette: A 75-year-old male patient is admitted with pneumonia. They are alert, oriented to person, place, and time, and engage in coherent conversation.  They live independently in their own home and manage all personal care. They have no personal history of cancer or other neoplastic diseases. The patient was diagnosed with cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection 10 years ago. They have no symptoms or diagnosis of heart failure and maintain an active lifestyle. They deny any history of stroke or transient ischemic attacks. They have normal kidney function with no history of renal disease. Their vital signs include a respiratory rate of 28, systolic BP of 85, pulse of 118 and temperature of 34.6. Their lab results show a pH of 7.31, BUN of 25, sodium of 135, glucose of 278, hematocrit of 28, PaO2 of 65. Chest radiograph reveals poor inspiratory effort, a consolidation in the left upper lobe and no effusions. What is their PSI/PORT score?

A 65-year-old male patient is admitted with pneumonia. The patient presents with confusion, disorientation, and inability to recognize family members.  They live independently in their own home and manage all personal care. The patient has a history of stage II colon cancer, diagnosed 5 years ago, and is currently in remission. The patient was diagnosed with cirrhosis due to chronic hepatitis C infection 10 years ago. The patient has congestive heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and takes daily diuretics. They deny any history of stroke or transient ischemic attacks. They have normal kidney function with no history of renal disease. Their vital signs include a respiratory rate of 28, systolic BP of 110, pulse of 130 and temperature of 34.6. Their lab results show a pH of 7.38, BUN of 25, sodium of 128, glucose of 220, hematocrit of 28, PaO2 of 55. Chest radiograph reveals bilateral infiltrates and a right-sided pleural effusion. What is their PSI/PORT score?
